name: Sacred Mijikenda Kaya Forests
description: Along roughly 200 km of Kenya's coast, ten patches of forest shelter the remains of kayas, fortified villages built by the Mijikenda people from the 16th century and abandoned by the 1940s. Today they are revered as the resting place of ancestors, and councils of elders still look after them. Visitors find quiet woodland that is a rare remnant of the original coastal forest, and prayer is still practised here.
